title: 3 Days in Rome
summary: Ancient ruins, Vatican treasures and long Roman dinners, planned so each day stays in one part of the city.
estimatedBudget: €450–600 per person, excluding flights and hotel

activities.title: Colosseum
activities.description: Enter with a timed ticket and walk the arena floor before the crowds build.

activities.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
activities.description: The same ticket covers both; follow the Via Sacra up to the palace ruins.

activities.title: Lunch in Monti
activities.description: Cacio e pepe at a small trattoria on Via Urbana.

activities.title: Capitoline Museums
activities.description: See the she-wolf statue and the best view over the Forum.

activities.title: Dinner in Trastevere
activities.description: Cross the river and eat in the cobbled lanes.

activities.title: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
activities.description: Book the first entry slot and allow three hours.

activities.title: St Peter's Basilica
activities.description: Entry is free; climb the dome for the view over the square.

activities.title: Lunch at Mercato Trionfale
activities.description: Street food and fresh fruit from the covered market.

activities.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
activities.description: Walk the ramparts and watch the sun set over the Tiber.

activities.title: Pizza in Prati
activities.description: Thin Roman-style pizza at a neighbourhood pizzeria.

activities.title: Pantheon
activities.description: Stand under the open oculus of the best-preserved Roman temple.

activities.title: Piazza Navona
activities.description: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and a morning espresso.

activities.title: Trevi Fountain
activities.description: Toss a coin over your shoulder to make sure you come back.

activities.title: Villa Borghese gardens
activities.description: Rent a bike and finish at the Pincio terrace.

activities.title: Farewell dinner in Testaccio
activities.description: The old market district where Romans eat the classics.

tips: Buy Colosseum and Vatican tickets online at least a week ahead.
Carry a refillable bottle; the street fountains have drinking water.
Churches ask for covered shoulders and knees.
Check opening days before you go; many museums close one day a week.
